subject: botany_2
question_text: Transpiration and Photosynthesis — a compromise. Explain.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.22, printed question 11. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: This is a chain of four steps, not a list. Write them in order — need water, open stomata, lose water, pull more water — because the last mark is for closing the loop.

steps.label: The plant needs water
steps.margin_note: Two or three lines. Establish the demand before anything opens.
lines: Photosynthesis needs a continuous supply of
A plant needs water all the time, and never
steps.why: The whole compromise starts from a demand that cannot be switched off, so the plant has no option of simply closing up and waiting.
common_mistakes: Saying water is needed only sometimes. The need is continuous.
Starting the answer at the stomata. The need for water comes first in the chain.
steps.memory_tip: The demand never stops, so the trade never stops either.

steps.label: Why stomata must open
steps.margin_note: Two lines: what has to come in, and what has to open to let it in.
lines: To photosynthesise, the plant must take in
So the plant opens its stomata to exchange
steps.why: Carbon dioxide can only enter through an open pore, so the stoma has to be open for photosynthesis to happen at all.
common_mistakes: Saying stomata open to release oxygen. They open mainly to take in carbon dioxide.
Leaving out gas exchange. That is the reason the pore opens.
steps.memory_tip: No open pore, no carbon dioxide, no sugar.

steps.label: What opening costs
steps.margin_note: Three lines. End on the pull, because the next step uses it.
lines: An open stoma also lets water escape by
The loss of water pulls more water up from the
steps.why: The same open pore that admits carbon dioxide lets water out, so the cost and the benefit cannot be separated — they share one opening.
common_mistakes: Treating the water loss as an accident. It is unavoidable once the pore is open.
Not linking the loss to the upward pull. That link is what makes the loss useful.
steps.memory_tip: One door, two directions: carbon dioxide in, water vapour out.

steps.label: The compromise
steps.margin_note: Close the loop and use the word 'compromise'. Four lines.

lines.text: One open pore serves both processes

lines: The water pulled up by transpiration is the
So the plant trades water loss for carbon gain.
steps.why: The loop closes because the water lost is what drags up the water used, so the cost pays for part of the benefit rather than just cancelling it.
common_mistakes: Ending without the word compromise. The question asks for it by name.
Saying the two processes are unrelated. They share the same open stoma.
steps.memory_tip: What the plant loses through the pore is what draws up what it needs.
